chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Mahboub, from Malik bin Atiyya, from Abdul A'ala bin Ayn, who said:

I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about a man who caught prey in the unrestricted area (al-Hill), so he tied it to the side of the Sanctuary (al-Haram). The prey went with its tie until it entered the Sanctuary, with the tie around its neck. The man pulled it with his rope until he brought it out of the Sanctuary, while the man himself was in the unrestricted area. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Its price and its flesh are prohibited, like the dead animal.'

key_terms.الْحَرَمِ: The Sanctuary (Mecca), where hunting is prohibited.
key_terms.الْحِلِّ: The unrestricted area for hunting, outside the sacred boundaries of Mecca.
key_terms.الْمَيْتَةِ: The dead animal (maytah), whose flesh is generally prohibited to eat.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prey that enters the Haram while tied and is pulled out by the hunter?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi details a specific juristic scenario where prey hunted in the unrestricted zone (al-Hill) enters the Sanctuary (al-Haram) while tied, and is subsequently pulled out by the hunter who remains outside. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the animal's value and flesh become prohibited (haram), equating its status to that of a dead animal (maytah) due to the breach of sanctity. This ruling highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the physical integrity of the animal's entry into the sacred space as a determinant for the validity of the hunt.
